The Amazon Black Friday deals are now live, where you can save on dozens of physical media items like video games, movies, board games, and seasons of great TV shows. One of these is the 4K Blu-ray version of A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms season 1, which is marked down to $22.99 from its original list price of $34.99.

A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms was 2026's first foray back into George R.R. Martin's fantasy world of Westeros. Based on the first of three prequel short stories also known as Tales of Dunk and Egg, HBO's show is an engaging and more comedically-toned version of their Game of Thrones world. There's still plenty of political and royal intrigue, violent action, and great world building, but it's a more standalone show compared to Game of Thrones and House of the Dragon.

Special Features

This 4K Blu-ray collection of the first season comes with all six episodes, and the following special features:

Inside the Episode (episodes 1-6)

A Knight in the Making featurette

Building a Knight of the Seven Kingdoms featurette

Blooper Reel

Welcome to a Knight of the Seven Kingdoms featurette

Meet Dunk and Meet Egg character pieces

Ashford Meadow Set Tour with Dexter Sol Ansell

We gave season one an 8 out of 10 in our review, saying it "may not have dragons, but A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms has plenty of heart, charm and humor -- and two endearing lead performances -- that make this a more than worthy watch". Season 2 is on the way, and we've learned a little more about what to expect.

Is streaming in 4K the same experience?

Like all HBO shows, A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms is available to stream in 4K with an HBO Max Premium subscription, but the picture quality you get from that just isn't going to be nearly as good as what you get with Blu-ray discs. This is largely because streaming services offer lower bitrates compared to 4K Blu-rays. A higher bitrate means a more detailed picture.

A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms (Tales of Dunk and Egg) Book

If you're curious about catching up the source material and checking out the second and third short stories (which seasons 2 and 3 will likely follow), the paperback version of the book is also pretty cheap on Amazon right now. Pick one up for $12.34, down from its usual $20 price tag.
